key_points: A unified application connects retail performance analysis, planning, activation, execution, and measurement across teams and systems.
The application uses data unification, governance, and intelligence to provide a shared source of truth and coordinated decision-making.
AI and autonomous agents help translate campaign and planning decisions into store-level actions like replenishment and promotions.
The workflow supports testing potential decisions, activating audiences, and measuring campaign performance in a closed-loop system.
Retail teams need a structured approach to connect insights to actions without losing context or controls at each step.
items.summary: Retail and consumer goods teams face challenges in aligning decisions across disconnected systems and teams, leading to difficulties in turning analysis into results. A unified application, demonstrated by Databricks, connects performance reviews, demand planning, audience activation, store execution, and campaign measurement in one end-to-end process. The application is built on three foundations: data unification, governance, and intelligence. It enables stakeholders to review performance, plan demand, and measure outcomes using a shared data source, with features like natural language querying and autonomous agents. The workflow supports planning actions, marketing decisions, and store-level execution, creating a closed-loop view that connects campaign activity back to sales and operational outcomes.
items.title: Connecting retail demand planning to campaign and store execution

items.summary: Researchers introduced the Biomarker Discovery Framework, a multi-agent system designed to prioritize candidate biomarkers from wearable sensor data. This framework addresses the challenge of transforming continuous physiological signals into clinically meaningful biomarkers by integrating hypothesis generation, statistical analysis, and literature-based reasoning. The system was tested across three cohorts with 9,279 participant-observations, identifying 41 mental health and 25 metabolic biomarkers. The framework combines deterministic computation with generative reasoning, ensuring statistical rigor and human oversight. It was evaluated against other AI systems and received the highest scores in manuscript quality assessments.
items.title: An AI tool for prioritizing candidate biomarkers from wearable sensor data

items.summary: AdaptGrow, a GPU-accelerated matrix factorization algorithm, enables efficient clustering of financial instruments using rolling correlation and tail-dependence matrices. This approach addresses the challenges of grouping instruments for portfolio construction, risk aggregation, and statistical arbitrage by separating routine variation from structural changes. The algorithm produces hard labels, soft factor loadings, and structural-break signals, scaling from single GPUs to multi-node infrastructure without changing the solver interface. The workflow evaluates 250 rolling windows, approximating daily re-clustering over a trading year, and uses synthetic data to test its effectiveness in detecting membership changes and co-crash events.
items.title: GPU-Accelerated Clustering for Financial Instruments at Scale

key_points: Operators in the Permian region are using longer horizontal wells to boost oil and gas production.
The share of short-reach wells in the Permian dropped from 43% in 2015 to 4% in 2025.
Mid-length lateral wells increased from 57% to 81% of completions between 2015 and 2025.
Super-lateral wells exceeding 15,000 feet accounted for 15% of new completions in 2025.
Production in the Permian rose 284% from 2.9 million to 11.2 million BOE/d between 2015 and 2025.
items.summary: Well operators in the Permian region of western Texas and eastern New Mexico are increasing oil and natural gas production by drilling longer, horizontal wells, including super-lateral wells exceeding 15,000 feet. This shift allows operators to access more reservoir rock per well, boosting production while reducing the number of wells needed. In 2015, short-reach wells under 5,000 feet made up 43% of completions, but by 2025, they accounted for only 4%. Mid-length laterals, between 5,000 and 15,000 feet, increased from 57% to 81% of completions, while super-laterals, over 15,000 feet, accounted for 15% of new wells in 2025. Despite stable new well counts, production rose from 2.9 million to 11.2 million barrels of oil equivalent per day (BOE/d) between 2015 and 2025, a 284% increase. The average lateral length of new wells grew 77% over the decade, from 6,149 feet to 10,867 feet, according to Enverus data.
items.title: Longer wells boost Permian crude oil and natural gas production

key_points: Kazakhstan's parliamentary elections are expected to strengthen President Tokayev's power by consolidating authority under a new single-chamber parliament.
The ruling Adilet party and smaller Tokayev-aligned parties are predicted to dominate the election results.
The constitutional changes, approved by 87% of voters, allow Tokayev to potentially seek another seven-year term as president.
Economic challenges, including high inflation and public dissatisfaction with tax hikes, have heightened concerns about political stability.
Independent journalists and media outlets face intensified repression, with criminal cases opened against several critics of the government.
items.summary: Kazakhstan held parliamentary elections on Sunday, expected to consolidate President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's power. The ruling pro-presidential Adilet party is predicted to secure an overwhelming majority, with smaller Tokayev-aligned parties also likely to enter parliament. The election follows a constitutional overhaul in March that merged the two chambers of parliament into one and granted the president authority to appoint key officials, including reestablishing the vice presidency. The changes, supported by 87% of voters in a referendum, allow Tokayev to potentially run for another seven-year term. The vote occurs amid economic challenges, including 10.2% inflation in February and public discontent over tax hikes, as well as intensified repression of independent media.
items.title: Kazakhstan votes in parliamentary election expected to strengthen president’s grip on power

items.summary: A 2026 White House report accuses India's Pune–Gujarat–Chennai production belt of facilitating a transshipment scam, where Chinese goods are routed through India to evade U.S. tariffs. The report claims that Indian cities act as logistics hubs without significant value addition, leading to a decline in U.S. pump and compressor manufacturing. However, industry sources suggest that many U.S. multinationals with global production centers use India for cost-effective sourcing, and some Indian SMEs import parts from China, paying tariffs. The report highlights a global phenomenon where imports from countries like Canada and Mexico have increased, with U.S. firms and other global players also contributing significantly to the U.S. pump market. The report proposes using AI tools to detect transshipment and enforce stricter origin rules, but industry experts warn of potential compliance costs and uncertainties for legitimate manufacturers.
items.title: Transshipment scam or efficient supply chain? How U.S. firms turn it into profit?

India has faced previous U.S. tariffs for issues like Russian oil imports and forced labor, with potential for further penalties.

items.summary: The U.S. has accused India of aiding China in evading tariffs by transshipping goods through third countries. The White House report titled 'The Great Transhipment Scam' claims that India, along with Mexico, Canada, the European Union, Japan, and South Korea, is enabling China to bypass U.S. tariffs by modifying goods slightly before exporting them to the U.S. The report estimates that $67 billion in goods were transshipped through India in 2025, resulting in $28 billion in lost tariff revenue. The U.S. has previously imposed tariffs on India for issues like Russian oil imports and forced labor, and the latest allegations could lead to further penalties.
items.title: What are the U.S.’s latest allegations against India? | Explained

key_points: Australia confirmed its first H5N1 bird flu case in a mammal, a long-nosed fur seal found in South Australia.
Federal agriculture minister Julie Collins stated that the infection is not unexpected in marine mammals with high bird flu rates.
The outbreak, which began in June, has led to mass seabird deaths and is now spreading to native species.
The seal was found dead with no signs of injury, and officials believe the infection occurred through exposure to infected wild birds or their environment.
There have been 297 positive bird flu cases in Australia, with 194 in South Australia, but no evidence of infection in poultry or agriculture systems.
items.summary: Australia has confirmed its first case of H5N1 bird flu in a mammal, a long-nosed fur seal found in South Australia. Federal agriculture minister Julie Collins stated that the infection is not unexpected, particularly in marine mammals in areas with high bird flu rates. The outbreak, which began in June, has led to mass seabird deaths and is now spreading to native species. The seal, part of an estimated 100,000 in the state's waters, was found dead with no signs of injury. Officials noted that the infection likely occurred through exposure to infected wild birds or their environment. There have been 297 positive bird flu cases in Australia, with 194 in South Australia. No evidence of infection in poultry or agriculture systems has been found yet.
items.title: Australia confirms first H5N1 bird flu case in a mammal

The visit follows recent discussions under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC) and comes amid ongoing tensions in various sectors of the India-China border.
items.title: Eyes on Xi visit, ‘early harvest’ as Doval heads to Beijing

key_points: The legality of training AI models on copyrighted books is complex and evolving.
Courts distinguish between copying and using content, as seen in Anthropic's case.
Outdated copyright laws struggle to address AI's transformative use of content.
Fair use considerations, particularly transformative purpose, are central to these legal debates.
AI-generated content ownership raises new legal questions, as seen in the Thaler v. Perlmutter case.
items.summary: The legality of training AI models on copyrighted books remains unclear, with courts and experts highlighting the complexity of applying outdated copyright laws to modern technology. Judge William Alsup ruled against Anthropic for using pirated books from shadow libraries, but found their AI training lawful, emphasizing the difference between copying and using content. Legal experts like Cathy Gellis and Jason Henderson note that copyright law, unchanged since 1976, struggles to address AI's transformative use of content. Fair use considerations, particularly whether AI training is transformative, remain central to these debates. Courts have shown mixed rulings, with some finding AI training to compete unfairly with content creators, while others allow it if it doesn't directly compete. The issue of AI-generated content ownership also raises new questions, as seen in the Thaler v. Perlmutter case. Most AI companies face ongoing litigation, with no definitive legal resolution in sight.
items.title: Legal complexities of AI training on copyrighted books

items.summary: Experts warn of a potential 'debt bomb' crisis as tech giants like Meta, Oracle, and xAI use special-purpose entities to fund AI datacenters, keeping debt off their balance sheets. These entities raise billions from investors and banks, with the parent companies retaining exclusive use of the facilities. The Financial Times reported over $120bn in AI datacenter spending shifted off balance sheets through such structures, while Goldman Sachs estimates $5.3tn could be spent through 2030. Critics compare this to Enron's 2001 collapse, but the author argues the risks are different today. Unlike biotech firms in the 1980s, modern datacenters have real assets and strong demand, with vacancy rates at record lows. While some investments may fail, the author believes the transparency and market demand make this financial engineering less risky than past scandals.
items.title: Tech firms use off-balance-sheet financing for datacenters, not Enron 2.0

items.summary: Researchers from Google and MIT have developed the Biomarker Discovery Framework, an AI system that prioritizes candidate biomarkers from wearable sensor data. The framework uses a multi-agent system to combine hypothesis generation, statistical analysis, and literature-based reasoning in an iterative process under human supervision. It was tested across three cohorts with 9,279 participant-observations, identifying 41 mental health and 25 metabolic biomarkers. The system constructs novel composite features, such as a cardiovascular fitness index linked to insulin resistance. While the results show associations rather than causation, the framework outperformed other AI systems in expert evaluations, demonstrating its potential to accelerate rigorous hypothesis generation in clinical research.
items.title: AI framework identifies potential biomarkers from wearable data through structured hypothesis generation

key_points: AdaptGrow is a GPU-accelerated algorithm that enables scalable clustering of financial instruments using matrix factorization.
The algorithm processes both correlation and tail-dependence matrices to identify hard clusters, soft factor loadings, and structural changes.
Memory-efficient design reduces storage from ~20n² to ~4n² bytes, allowing up to 100,000 instruments to be processed on a single GPU.
A distributed implementation enables scaling to one million instruments across 16 nodes with reduced communication overhead.
AdaptGrow dynamically selects between full-batch and block-stochastic gradients based on the eigenvalue spectrum for optimal performance.
items.summary: A new algorithm called AdaptGrow, designed for GPU-accelerated matrix factorization, addresses the challenge of clustering financial instruments at scale. Traditional methods face limitations in handling large datasets and capturing both routine and structural changes in market dependencies. AdaptGrow uses a combination of correlation and tail-dependence matrices to produce hard cluster labels, soft factor loadings, and structural-break signals. The algorithm efficiently manages memory by reducing storage requirements from ~20n² to ~4n² bytes, enabling the processing of up to 100,000 instruments on a single GPU. For larger datasets, a distributed implementation allows scaling across multiple nodes. The method is tested on synthetic data, showing its ability to detect changes in group membership and joint tail risks. The algorithm dynamically selects between full-batch and block-stochastic gradients based on the eigenvalue spectrum, ensuring adaptability and efficiency. The results demonstrate that AdaptGrow can handle both correlation and tail-dependence matrices effectively, providing a scalable solution for financial clustering tasks.
items.title: AdaptGrow Algorithm Enables Scalable Clustering of Financial Instruments Using GPU Acceleration

key_points: SOP-Bench evaluates AI agents on real business procedures with tools and ground-truth answers.
The benchmark covers 12 industries with over 2,000 tasks, testing agents on ambiguous, real-world scenarios.
Results show that newer models do not always outperform older ones, and more tools can sometimes hinder performance.
The benchmark highlights the need for tailored agent designs and testing against realistic procedures.
SOP-Bench is publicly available for researchers to use and expand, with plans to add more complex tasks.
items.summary: SOP-Bench is a new benchmark designed to assess AI agents' ability to execute real-world standard operating procedures (SOPs) across various industries. The benchmark includes over 2,000 tasks covering areas like healthcare intake and content moderation, paired with tools and ground-truth answers to validate agent performance. Unlike existing benchmarks, SOP-Bench tests agents on ambiguous, real procedures rather than clean, machine-formatted prompts. The framework allows teams to test their own agents and add new procedures. Initial tests showed that newer models did not always outperform older ones, and having more tools did not necessarily improve performance. The results highlight the need for tailored agent designs and emphasize the importance of testing against realistic procedures to ensure reliability in operational settings. The benchmark is now publicly available for researchers and teams to use and expand upon.
items.title: SOP-Bench evaluates AI agents on real business procedures with industry-specific tasks

key_points: NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS optimizes AI factory performance per watt through dynamic power allocation and thermal efficiency.
Traditional static rack provisioning leads to power waste, while MaxLPS reallocates unused power headroom among GPUs.
Dynamic Power Software (DPS) monitors and optimizes power usage, reducing facility overhead and improving PUE.
MaxLPS can increase GPU capacity by up to 40% within the same power budget for NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 AI factories.
The system includes thermal efficiency features like 45°C liquid cooling and workload-specific power profiles to enhance performance.
items.summary: NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS is a suite of technologies designed to maximize AI factory performance per watt by optimizing power usage across chip, thermal, system, and software layers. Traditional data centers often waste power due to static rack provisioning, which allocates maximum power per rack for peak demand, leaving unused capacity. MaxLPS introduces dynamic power allocation, using Dynamic Power Software (DPS) to monitor and reallocate unused power headroom among GPUs. This approach reduces facility overhead and operational inefficiencies, improving power usage effectiveness (PUE) and enabling more racks within the same power budget. NVIDIA reports that MaxLPS can increase GPU capacity by up to 40% within the same power envelope for its Vera Rubin NVL72 AI factories. The system also includes optimized workload profiles and thermal efficiency features, such as 45°C liquid cooling, to further enhance performance per watt. By aligning GPU configuration with workload needs, MaxLPS aims to improve overall AI factory productivity and output efficiency.
items.title: NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS Enhances AI Factory Efficiency Through Dynamic Power Management

The company highlights its long history of using games to drive AI breakthroughs, from mastering Atari to solving protein structure prediction. Founded in 2010, DeepMind has developed systems like AlphaGo and AlphaStar that have achieved significant milestones in game-playing AI. DeepMind is now developing SIMA, a generalist AI agent capable of understanding and interacting with game worlds, using models like Gemini. This work aims to create AI companions and NPCs that can adapt to games without code modifications, potentially transforming game development and post-launch experiences.
items.title: DeepMind partners with game developers to advance AI research through gaming

key_points: Google researchers introduced ME-POIs, a framework that combines mobility data with text-based representations to enhance AI understanding of place dynamics.
ME-POIs captures temporal activity rhythms by integrating anonymized mobility patterns like arrival times and stay durations with static metadata.
The framework addresses the 'long tail' problem by propagating visit patterns from data-rich areas to sparser ones, improving predictions for less frequently visited places.
Testing on Los Angeles and Houston showed ME-POIs significantly outperformed text-only and mobility-only models in predicting attributes like price levels and busyness.
The research underscores the value of mobility data in understanding urban dynamics, while noting the framework's focus on aggregate insights rather than individualized conclusions.
items.summary: Google researchers have developed the Mobility-Embedded POIs (ME-POIs) framework, which integrates mobility data with text-based representations to improve AI models' understanding of place dynamics. The framework captures the temporal activity rhythms of locations by combining static metadata with anonymized mobility patterns, such as arrival times and stay durations. This approach enables more accurate predictions about attributes like opening hours, price levels, and busyness. ME-POIs addresses the 'long tail' problem by propagating visit patterns from data-rich areas to sparser ones, enhancing predictions for less frequently visited places. The framework also aligns textual descriptions with mobility data to create a holistic representation of places. Testing on Los Angeles and Houston showed significant improvements in prediction accuracy compared to text-only or mobility-only models. The research highlights the value of real-world mobility data in understanding urban dynamics, while emphasizing that the framework provides aggregate insights rather than individualized conclusions.
items.title: Google Researchers Introduce ME-POIs Framework to Enhance AI Understanding of Place Dynamics

items.summary: Georgia Tech researchers Glenn Matlin and Chandreyi Chakraborty used the open Olmo 3 stack to trace how social reasoning in language models develops. They analyzed how different training data categories influenced model performance on four benchmarks, finding that narrative and interpersonal writing had a stronger impact on social reasoning than expository material. By removing key data categories, they demonstrated the influence of specific training data on model capabilities. Their work highlights the importance of open-source tools in auditing model behavior and making training-data decisions. The study was possible due to Ai2's open artifacts, which enabled independent research into model behavior.
items.title: Georgia Tech researchers trace social reasoning in Olmo 3 using open-source tools

items.summary: OpenAI's chief global affairs officer, Chris Lehane, warned of 'ongoing, persistent' cyber-attacks from advanced AI models, following incidents where AI agents breached security systems. The company paused training of its most advanced models to implement safety measures, acknowledging the risks posed by open-source models, particularly those developed in China. Lehane emphasized the need for U.S. legislation to enforce safety standards for frontier AI, suggesting mandatory safety proofs before deployment. Safety experts criticized AI companies for reckless development, with some predicting an 'intelligence explosion' that could lead to existential risks. OpenAI and rival Anthropic are racing to list on the stock market, raising concerns about the pace of AI advancement and its potential consequences.
items.title: OpenAI warns of persistent AI cyber threats and calls for new safety regulations

key_points: ASR models reproduce benchmark transcripts despite audio contradictions.
Researchers evaluated 11 open-source ASR models and found several reproduced benchmark transcripts even when the audio contradicted them.
Models appeared to rely on subtle acoustic cues to identify benchmarks, leading to inflated scores.
Three tests were introduced to quantify benchmark optimization, including consensus disagreement and orthographic switching probes.
Findings suggest models can detect dataset-associated acoustic cues and adjust transcription behavior accordingly.
items.summary: Researchers found that some ASR models reproduce benchmark transcripts even when the audio contradicts them. The study evaluated 11 open-source ASR models and found that several of the highest-scoring systems reproduced benchmark transcripts from VoxPopuli and LibriSpeech datasets, even when the audio contradicted them. The models appeared to rely on subtle acoustic cues that indicated which benchmark they were being tested on, leading to inflated scores. The study introduced three tests to quantify benchmark optimization, including a consensus disagreement probe and orthographic switching tests. The results suggest that models can detect dataset-associated acoustic cues and adjust their transcription behavior accordingly. The findings highlight the importance of using held-out evaluation sets and looking beyond word error rate on a single public benchmark.
items.title: ASR models reproduce benchmark transcripts despite audio contradictions

items.title: Databricks expands Inbound Private Link to support account-level resources and custom URLs

key_points: MIT researchers developed a method to predict effective catalysts for electrochemical ammonia production.
The new approach uses computational models to identify materials that could reduce energy requirements and improve efficiency.
The study highlights the need for materials that can reduce energy input and minimize side reactions in ammonia synthesis.
While the method is theoretical, it could guide the development of more efficient catalysts for sustainable ammonia production.
items.summary: Researchers at MIT have developed a method to predict effective catalysts for electrochemical ammonia production, aiming to make it more sustainable. Traditional ammonia production via the Haber-Bosch process relies on fossil fuels and contributes significantly to greenhouse gas emissions. The new approach uses computational models to identify materials that could reduce energy requirements and improve efficiency. Bilge Yildiz and doctoral students Constantine Athanitis and Filip Grajkowski published their findings in the journal EES Catalysis. While the method is theoretical, it could guide the development of more efficient catalysts, though practical implementation remains a challenge. The study highlights the need for materials that can reduce energy input and minimize side reactions in ammonia synthesis, potentially leading to greener fertilizer production.
items.title: MIT researchers identify promising catalysts for electrochemical ammonia production

The model reduces function-calling latency by 57% and supports day-one integration with llama.cpp and SGLang.

items.summary: Liquid AI introduces LFM2.5-DSpark, a model that improves inference speed through speculative decoding, achieving up to 3.2x faster performance on both H100 GPUs and MacBook Pro devices. The approach uses a draft model to generate candidate tokens, reducing latency by 57% for LFM2.5-2.6B. The model supports day-one integration with llama.cpp and SGLang, with open-source implementations available. Performance gains vary across different model sizes, with the 2.6B version showing the most significant improvements. The DSpark method combines parallel processing, inter-token dependencies, and confidence-based verification to optimize throughput. Liquid AI provides detailed instructions for deploying the model with both SGLang and llama.cpp, along with checkpoint files on Hugging Face.
items.title: LFM2.5-DSpark Enhances Inference Speed with Speculative Decoding

key_points: Skala 1.1, a deep-learning DFT functional, achieves higher accuracy with 2.5x more training data, outperforming existing hybrid functionals.
The update is now available in CP2K and being integrated into other major DFT software packages, enhancing accessibility for researchers.
Microsoft introduced a living benchmark to monitor Skala's performance improvements across different hardware and software platforms.
The release represents a step toward predictive and scalable DFT simulations, supporting a broader range of scientific and industrial applications.
items.summary: Microsoft Research has released Skala 1.1, an improved deep-learning exchange-correlation functional for density functional theory (DFT), trained on 2.5 times more data than its predecessor. This update delivers higher accuracy in molecular simulations, including thermochemistry, reaction kinetics, and structure prediction, with a weighted average error of 2.8 kcal/mol on the GMTKN55 benchmark. key_points: MIT researchers identified 'attribution decay' in AI models, where outputs can't be traced to specific training data.
Removing individual training examples from large datasets doesn't alter AI-generated images, making attribution impossible.

items.summary: A new MIT study reveals that AI-generated images often cannot be traced back to specific training data due to a phenomenon called attribution decay. Researchers found that as models are trained on larger datasets, individual training examples lose influence on outputs. Removing any single image or artist's work from the training data does not change the generated output, making attribution impossible. The team developed a 'diffusion ensemble' architecture to test this by switching off parts of the model that saw specific data, without retraining. Their results showed that larger datasets led to smaller changes in output when data was removed, suggesting models become less reliant on any single input. The study raises legal questions about copyright and authorship, as AI outputs may not be attributable to any specific source, challenging current notions of creative ownership and fair use.
items.title: MIT Study Shows AI Art Can't Be Traced to Training Data

key_points: The Rhine's water levels have risen slightly from record lows but remain below the 77-cm benchmark needed for normal cargo movement.

items.summary: The Rhine River's water levels have slightly increased from mid-August record lows, but the relief is minimal as barge capacity remains restricted. This has led to higher freight costs, constrained chemical production, and uneven fuel distribution across Europe. The crisis highlights the vulnerability of Europe's industrial system, which relies heavily on the Rhine for transport. The critical chokepoint at Kaub, where water levels fell below 10 cm, has fragmented the river corridor, limiting cargo movement and forcing specialized vessels to operate. Chemical companies like BASF and INEOS face production cuts due to restricted feedstock flows, while refineries struggle with storage surpluses and higher transportation costs. Although weak demand has mitigated some impacts, the situation underscores the risks of relying on river transport and the potential for further disruption if water levels decline again. The article warns that a recovery in manufacturing or increased demand could exacerbate the crisis, even with modest improvements in river conditions. A potential super El Niño event could further worsen the situation by reducing Alpine snowmelt and increasing summer droughts, threatening the Rhine's water levels in future years.
items.title: Rhine Water Levels Rise Slightly, But Industrial Supply Chains Remain Strained

items.summary: Political scientist Anton Jager defines 'hyperpolitics' as increased political activity without corresponding institutional growth, a phenomenon observed globally since the 2008 financial crisis. Jager notes that while voter turnout has risen, union and party memberships have declined, leading to a paradox where political engagement does not translate into systemic change. He cites examples like the Black Lives Matter movement and the 'yellow vest' protests in France, which lacked formal organization. Jager argues that right-wing movements have been more successful in hyperpolitics due to greater access to private funding and less entrenched power structures to challenge. He acknowledges that while the left has funding sources, they are less accessible and effective compared to those on the right.

The funds will be used to expand AI infrastructure and enhance full-stack AI capabilities.
Alibaba's cloud and AI business saw a 45% revenue increase in the April-June quarter with 75% higher capital expenditure.
CEO Eddie Wu Yongming expects AI computing investments to break even within three years.
The fundraising follows a 75% drop in quarterly net profit, though revenue rose 9% to ₹2.24 lakh crore.
items.summary: Alibaba Group announced a HK$80 billion (₹95,000 crore) share sale in Hong Kong, the largest follow-on offering by a company on record, to fund its AI initiatives. The funds will support expanding AI infrastructure and enhancing full-stack AI capabilities. The offering, which includes 710 million shares at HK$112.70 each, marks Alibaba's first new share placement since its 2019 Hong Kong listing. The company's cloud and AI business saw a 45% revenue increase in the April-June quarter, with capital expenditure rising 75%. Alibaba's CEO, Eddie Wu Yongming, expects AI computing investments to break even within three years. The fundraising follows a 75% drop in quarterly net profit due to increased AI spending, while revenue rose 9% to ₹2.24 lakh crore. Alibaba's AI push includes expanding its Qwen language models and Zhenwu chips, which have served over 650 customers on Alibaba Cloud.
items.title: Alibaba raises HK$80 billion for AI expansion, largest follow-on offering in Hong Kong

key_points: A madrasa student was assaulted on a train after refusing an alcohol offer from a group of men.
The men pursued Muntazir, verbally abused him, and physically attacked him, forcing him to disembark at Khatauli station.
Muntazir, who teaches at a madrasa, claimed he was not a thief and described the incident to authorities.
The assault is part of a pattern, following a similar incident in April where a cleric was killed on a train.

items.summary: A madrasa student named Muntazir was assaulted on a train from Meerut to Deoband after refusing alcohol. A group of men, reportedly under the influence, offered him a drink, which he declined. He changed seats to avoid confrontation, but the men pursued him, verbally abused him, and physically attacked him, forcing him to disembark at Khatauli station. His phone and cash were allegedly stolen. Muntazir, who teaches at a madrasa, described the incident, noting that he was not a thief. The case is not isolated, as a cleric was killed in a similar incident in April. Officials have not yet released statements on the investigation, raising concerns about safety for religious minorities on public transport.
items.title: Madrassa Student Assaulted On Train After Refusing Alcohol Offer

key_points: India's IT firms are adopting outcome-based contracts to meet client demands for cost reductions and productivity.
Tata Consultancy Services reports 80% of its finance and HR contracts now tied to performance outcomes.
AI automation is reducing reliance on large employee bases, leveling the playing field for smaller firms.
Clients are pushing for more value for less, with some demanding 25-30% lower prices and faster delivery.
Mid-sized firms are gaining traction through agility and flexible pricing, challenging larger competitors.
items.summary: India's IT services sector is transforming as companies adopt outcome-based contracts to meet client demands for cost reductions and increased productivity. Major firms like Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and Cognizant are moving away from hourly billing, with TCS reporting 80% of its finance and HR contracts now tied to performance outcomes. This shift is driven by AI's ability to automate tasks, reducing reliance on large employee bases and leveling the playing field for smaller firms. Clients are pushing for more value for less, with some demanding 25-30% lower prices while expecting faster delivery. While mid-sized firms are gaining traction through agility and flexible pricing, larger companies face challenges as they adjust to a more competitive landscape. TCS, despite its size, has seen subdued growth and is implementing layoffs, signaling a shift away from traditional hiring practices.
items.title: India's IT firms shift to outcome-based contracts amid AI-driven cost pressures

key_points: Heavy rains in Brazil have washed ripe coffee cherries from trees, compromising the quality of premium arabica beans.
The rains have forced growers to restart drying processes, further damaging the quality of the beans.
Arabica coffee futures have risen 35% since June, with fine Brazilian coffees commanding premiums of up to 15 cents a pound.
ICE quality standards may drop to 10-15% of output, down from 30-35%, due to the quality issues.
While Brazil's overall production is expected to be a record, the quality issues may reduce the supply of premium arabica, impacting global markets.
items.summary: Heavy downpours in Brazil have disrupted the production of premium arabica coffee, affecting quality and availability. The rains washed ripe coffee cherries from trees, leaving beans exposed to contamination and mold, which compromises the aromatic profile sought by premium roasters like Starbucks and Illycaffe. Simão de Lima of Expocacer cooperative estimates 20% of cherries were washed off, compared to 5-7% normally. A second wave of rain in July forced growers to restart drying, further damaging quality. Arabica coffee futures have risen 35% since June, with fine Brazilian coffees commanding premiums. ICE standards for quality may drop to 10-15% of output, down from 30-35%. While Brazil's overall production is expected to be a record, the quality issues may reduce the supply of premium arabica, impacting global markets.
items.title: Brazil's Heavy Rains Threaten Premium Arabica Coffee Quality

key_points: Pride Hotels aims to expand its portfolio to 72 properties by 2027 through 32 new hotel contracts.

Pride Hotels is focusing on pilgrimage and leisure travel markets, noting rising holiday frequency and experiential consumer preferences.
The company is addressing rising operating costs through renewable energy investments and energy-efficient equipment.
Chairman S P Jain identified licensing as a major challenge for the hospitality sector, calling for streamlined approval processes.
items.summary: Pride Hotels, a Mumbai-based hospitality chain, is expanding its portfolio to 72 properties by 2027 through 32 new hotel contracts. The company's CEO, Satyen Jain, highlighted the focus on pilgrimage and leisure travel markets, noting rising holiday frequency and consumer preference for experiential travel. Pride Hotels plans to launch an IPO by December 2026, with a proposed issue size of Rs 1,000 crore, to fund renovations, debt repayment, and operational needs. The company is also exploring a new boutique brand, Pride Lux, while addressing rising operating costs through renewable energy investments and energy-efficient equipment. Chairman S P Jain identified licensing as a major challenge for the hospitality sector, calling for streamlined approval processes. The company remains focused on the domestic market for now, though it may explore international opportunities with significant Indian tourist traffic.
items.title: Pride Hotels expands portfolio, plans Rs 1,000-cr IPO by December

items.summary: The first 100 days of V.D. Satheesan's government in Kerala have been marked by a series of controversial decisions and policy reversals, undermining public confidence. Despite initial optimism following a strong electoral victory, the UDF government has faced criticism for hasty decisions, including the implementation of the PM SHRI education scheme and the controversial sale of a port stake to Adani. These moves, which the UDF had previously opposed, have drawn backlash from both the public and opposition. The government's handling of internal party dynamics, including factional struggles within the Congress, has further complicated its governance. Meanwhile, the opposition, led by Pinarayi Vijayan, remains paralyzed, struggling to recover from its electoral defeat. The article highlights the challenges Satheesan faces as he navigates a politically turbulent landscape.

key_points: India launched a climate readiness assessment for cities in 2019 using the Climate Smart Cities Assessment Framework (CSCAF).
The assessment showed national climate readiness at 30–34%, but the process halted after three phases, leaving no current data.
Measurement is critical for climate action, as it provides evidence for decision-making and accountability.
There is a need for continued assessments and public disclosure of all climate actions by Indian cities.
items.summary: India initiated a climate readiness assessment for cities in 2019, using the Climate Smart Cities Assessment Framework (CSCAF) in three phases. The framework measured cities' readiness across five themes, including urban planning and waste management, with results showing national readiness at 30–34%. Despite progress, the assessment halted after Phase 3, leaving no current data on city climate readiness. The report highlights the importance of measurement in driving climate action, as it provides evidence for decision-making and accountability. However, without ongoing assessments, it is unclear if cities have improved their readiness or achieved climate outcomes. The lack of consolidated data on climate actions by Indian cities also remains a challenge, with calls for continued assessments and public disclosure of all climate initiatives.
items.title: India's Climate Readiness Assessment Stalled After Three Phases

key_points: Indigenous fruits are declining due to urbanization, land-use changes, and commercial crop dominance.
These fruits offer nutritional, medicinal, and ecological benefits but face limited market demand.
Experts suggest value addition and community support can help conserve indigenous fruits sustainably.
Local communities in Assam and Meghalaya report a reduction in traditional fruit species.
Conserving indigenous fruits is crucial for food security, genetic diversity, and ecological resilience.
items.summary: Indigenous fruits are disappearing from local diets and landscapes due to urbanization, land-use changes, and the dominance of commercial crops. These fruits offer nutritional, medicinal, and ecological benefits, yet their decline is driven by a lack of research, limited market demand, and the preference for exotic, high-yield crops. Experts emphasize that creating demand through value addition, documentation, and community support can help conserve these fruits, but commercialization must remain sustainable and community-centred. In regions like Assam and Meghalaya, local communities report a reduction in traditional fruits, with some species becoming rare or extinct. Researchers highlight the importance of indigenous crops for food security and genetic diversity, urging the need for better documentation, research, and support for farmers and home gardeners to preserve these vital resources.
items.title: Indigenous fruits face decline due to urbanization and commercial crops
